text:
cara: Heads up — eu-west3 NVMe latency spikes during large checkpoint windows, GPUs failing attach with PREEMPT. IOWAIT looks high. Anyone seeing this in traces?
devon: saw the alert 3m ago, attach_failure rate bumped ~2.7%. Patterns show lots of tiny 4-8k fsyncs from checkpoint-writer + janitor compaction running concurrently. Queue depth climbing.
Storage Bot: ALERT nvme_iops(scratchpool-euw3) sustained >115k for 6m. nvme_p99=135ms, avg_lat=5.1ms, attach_failures increased.
arnold: Quick thought — we should reduce janitor concurrency and try to batch small writes from checkpointing. Can we do a fast canary with a janitor rate cap + a write-aggregation layer (tmpfs) on a handful of nodes?
lee: Agree. Proposed canary config: `janitor.max_ops_per_sec: 750`, `janitor.concurrency: 2`, `checkpoint.agg_tmpfs: true` on gnode-euw3-61..66 (6 nodes). Also set `vm.dirty_ratio=3` and `vm.dirty_background_bytes=33554432` to limit sync storms.
cara: Canary risks: throttling janitor delays cleanup -> disk pressure increases longer term; tmpfs consumes RAM and pushes swap if misconfigured. Need rollback criteria.
sre-oncall: I'll run the canary and monitor. Rollback if attach_success <= 99% or nvme_p99 > 100ms for 10m.
arnold: How to implement tmpfs aggregator quickly: mount tmpfs at `/var/checkpoints/agg`, run a tiny daemon that moves files out via `rsync --partial --bwlimit=20000 --remove-source-files` and `ionice -c2 -n7` to smooth writes.
devon: Can we capture blktrace on the canary nodes for 10m window? Command: ```sudo blktrace -d /dev/nvme0n1 -w 600 -o /tmp/blktrace.out && blkparse -i /tmp/blktrace.out -v > /tmp/blkparse.txt``` That will help show write coalescing.
Storage Bot: RUNBOOK snippet: if nvme_iops drop <30% within 3m of throttle -> escalate; if attach_fail_rate spikes >5% rollback immediately.
cara: Rollout steps (short):
  1) apply helm override for janitor to gnode-euw3-61..66
  2) enable agg tmpfs and start rsync daemon (systemd unit)
  3) apply kernel tunables via ansible on those hosts
  4) start blktrace capture for 15m
  5) monitor metrics: nvme_iops, nvme_qdepth, nvme_p99, attach_success, janitor_ops
  6) if stable 2h -> expand to 20 nodes, 24h -> region rollout decision
sre-oncall: Starting canary now on gnode-euw3-61..66. Will post 10m update.
Storage Bot: ACTION: throttle applied to gnode-euw3-61..66. nvme_iops fell 112k -> 38k in 75s. nvme_p99 dropped to 26ms. attach_success in canary moved 96.5% -> 99.8%.
lee: Nice. Please save blktrace output and attach to ticket. This gives a strong signal that write burst overlap was the root cause.
devon: FYI PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/helm/pulls/2389 — adds tmpfs aggregator unit + janitor rate flags.
arnold: Cost note: tmpfs + rsync increases RAM usage and network egress modestly; rough runway cost estimate for full region ~ $140/day (ephemeral egress + CPU). Adding to RFC.
sre-oncall: 1h steady, metrics holding. Will run a 4h soak and then propose expanding to 20 nodes. If any regressions we revert helm to previous values immediately.
cara: Good work. After region rollout we should design a persistent write-aggregator service (long-term) that can be configured per workload and avoids per-host tmpfs hacks. Keeping this thread as canary run log for the follow-up RFC.
